description:
FOUND s463av while measuring #950 (the runtime's optimize policy), and it is
the finding that made two of the eighteen bench rows unmeasurable rather than
slow: with ONE `(declaim (optimize (speed 3)))` at the top of
`cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`, `pack("N n C a3", …)` dies with

    p-pack: cl/pcl-pack.lisp not found in <root>/cl/

while `cl/pcl-pack.lisp` is sitting in that very directory.

THE MECHANISM.  `p-load-extension` answers T for the load that ACTUALLY
happened and NIL for every later call (its body is `(unless (gethash name
*pcl-loaded-extensions*) … (return-from … t))` falling through to `nil`).  So a
self-loading stub gets exactly ONE chance: the extension file it just `load`ed
REDEFINES the stub's own name with the real implementation, and the delegation
must reach THAT definition.  One more trip through the stub raises the
"not found" error on a file that is present.

`p-pack` delegated with `(apply #'p-pack template args)` and `p-unpack` with
`(p-unpack template str)` — both DIRECT references to the name being defined.
SBCL converts a `defun`'s reference to its own name into a LOCAL call whenever
the policy has `(> speed debug)`.  At the runtime's actual policy (SBCL's
default, speed 1 = debug 1) the conversion does not fire, the reference stays a
global call through the fdefinition, and the redefinition is picked up — which
is why this has always worked.  Raise the file's speed above its debug and the
call becomes "jump back to the top of this same code", the stub re-enters
itself, `p-load-extension` answers NIL the second time, and the error fires.

THE OTHER SPELLING WAS ALREADY RIGHT — this is rule 11 exactly.  The
`%pcl-def-ext-stub` macro (mro's seven entry points, warnings, xs) delegates
with `(apply (symbol-function ',name) args)`, which is a fdefinition lookup
SBCL cannot fold into a local call.  Two spellings of one mechanism; the odd
ones out were the two hand-written ones, and they were hand-written because the
macro was defined LOWER IN THE FILE than pack/unpack.

MEASURED, both directions:
  * speed-3 probe runtime, unpatched:  `p-pack: cl/pcl-pack.lisp not found`
  * same probe with `(apply (symbol-function 'p-pack) …)`: prints 10, correct.

SHIPPED s463av.  `%pcl-def-ext-stub` moved UP to just above the pack section
(one definition, where it used to be defined twice-over in effect: once as a
macro and once by hand), and `p-pack` / `p-unpack` are now
`(%pcl-def-ext-stub p-pack "pcl-pack")` / `(… p-unpack "pcl-pack")`.
`p-unpack`'s `$_` default lives on the REAL definition in `cl/pcl-pack.lisp`
(`(defun p-unpack (template &optional (str $_)) …)`), which is the one every
call after the first reaches, so the stub's `&rest` passes the caller's actual
arguments straight through and the default is applied exactly where it was.

The error text changes from `p-pack: …` to `pcl-pack: …` (the macro names the
EXTENSION, not the entry point); nothing in `Pl/t` or `tools/` reads it.

GUARD: `Pl/t/extension-preamble-01.t` — a source invariant, because the bug is
only OBSERVABLE at a policy the tree does not compile at.  It asserts that the
runtime defines `%pcl-def-ext-stub` exactly once and that every
`p-load-extension` call site in the runtime is inside it, so a future
hand-written stub fails the row instead of quietly re-acquiring the
self-call.  Inverse-verified on a 6e6f191 worktree.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE PROBE: this is a landmine under any future policy
change to the runtime — including #950's own subject — and the failure it
produces is a confident lie about a file that exists.
subject: The self-loading extension stubs p-pack/p-unpack delegated by a SELF-CALL, so they were correct only at the runtime's current optimize policy (SHIPPED s463av)
